methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter retrospective study through USMIRC comparing bortezomib-lenalidomide (VR) vs lenalidomide alone (R) maintenance post-ASCT in high-risk MM (del17p, t4;14, t14;16, t14;20, ±1q gain). Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing for PFS/OS. Median 91-month follow-up. Baseline characteristics well-balanced. Limitations: retrospective non-randomized design; treatment selection bias inherent; no statistical significance achieved despite numerical trends.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort comparison (LoE 2b) addressing clinical practice gap regarding maintenance strategy in understudied HRMM population. VR showed numerical but not statistically significant PFS improvement (51 vs 36 months), limiting clinical actionability.

reporting_quality.justification: Real-world multicenter analysis clearly describing cohorts, baseline characteristics, treatment exposure. Kaplan-Meier curves and statistical comparisons presented. Limitations: retrospective methodology; incomplete data on induction/post-transplant details; no data repository statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Multicenter real-world analysis comparing VR vs R maintenance in HRMM; lenalidomide-based maintenance established standard. VR intensity not novel; findings suggest lack of benefit over standard approach.

writing_presentation.justification: Organized multicenter real-world analysis addressing clinical practice question. Methods, results clearly presented. Discussion appropriately notes need for prospective trials with novel targets.

key_strengths: Multicenter real-world data (USMIRC) addressing practical maintenance question in understudied HRMM population with significant prognostic markers
Well-balanced baseline characteristics between VR and R groups
Extended median 91-month follow-up enabling long-term outcome assessment
key_concerns: Retrospective non-randomized design with inherent treatment selection bias; no statistical significance achieved for primary endpoints (PFS p>0.05, OS p>0.05) despite numerical trends
Small subgroup analysis: limited number of HRMM patients with specific cytogenetic markers; inadequate power for definitive conclusions
Findings negative for VR benefit over standard lenalidomide; conclusions recommend prospective trials rather than validating current practice intensification
chief_reviewer.rationale: Real-world multicenter study with negative findings for VR intensification, limited by retrospective design and non-significant outcomes. Appropriate for tier 4 specialty journals as hypothesis-generating work supporting prospective trials.
